evidence.title: Maestro SSH remote execution
evidence.locator: Overview; Configuring SSH Remotes; Per-Session Configuration; Collaborating over SSH; Limitations
evidence.finding: Agents run on user-provided SSH hosts; remote CLI installation and credentials are prerequisites. Optional per-session shared history writes per-hostname JSONL files to the remote project, shown with hostname badges.

evidence.locator: Groups; Tokens; Export; What is NOT tracked
evidence.finding: Current dashboard sections describe token/cost aggregation and export, but the final exclusions still say tokens/costs are not aggregated. The contradiction remains unresolved.

evidence.title: Maestro Maestro CLI
evidence.locator: Sending messages; Global Flags; Auto Run
evidence.finding: CLI sends/resumes agent sessions, runs playbooks and exposes structured JSON and failure codes. Some commands require the app reachable.

evidence.title: Maestro Group Chat
evidence.locator: How it Works; Moderator role; Availability
evidence.finding: A moderator coordinates named agents over multiple turns and routes results. Participants do not automatically see each other replies.

evidence.title: Maestro Remote control
evidence.finding: A browser/phone client uses the full host UI. URL token grants full control; LIVE-off returns loopback-only and rotates the token.

evidence.title: Maestro Git and worktrees
evidence.locator: Git menu; Worktree agents; Setup scripts
evidence.finding: Git log/diff and PR actions integrate with nested worktree agents. Setup scripts run before first agent prompt, on the selected local/SSH host.

evidence.title: Maestro Memories
evidence.finding: Claude-only project memory viewer reads/edits/deletes Markdown memory; other providers do not expose this panel.

evidence.title: Maestro History
evidence.finding: Timestamped AUTO/USER/AGENT/CUE entries can be searched and reopened by session ID; immutability is not established.

evidence.title: Maestro Configuration
evidence.finding: Update check sends UUID/version/platform/theme telemetry, disabled with update checking. Folder sync warns against simultaneous devices and has no conflict resolution.

evidence.title: Maestro Agent resilience
evidence.locator: Strategies; Never retry; Status card; Quit
evidence.finding: Provider overload/quota errors retry with visible cards; credential/permission/crash failures do not. Pending retries do not survive app quit.

evidence.title: Maestro Cue on a server
evidence.finding: Current public docs describe a source-built Linux/systemd or container runner for exported pipelines and agents. It runs unattended in YOLO, with server-side credentials. The same path is absent at the pinned repository revision.

evidence.title: Maestro v1.0.2
evidence.finding: v1.0.2 is the sampled stable release; the same feed also has v1.1.0-RC. Current pinned documentation can include prerelease behavior.

evidence.title: Maestro README.md
evidence.locator: How it works; Features; Quick start
evidence.finding: Maestro passes prompts to locally configured provider CLIs and inherits their MCP tools, skills, permissions and authentication. Desktop installation supports user-owned operation. Its documentation MCP server searches docs rather than controlling tasks.

evidence.title: Maestro docs/group-chat.md
evidence.locator: Agent availability; Message queue; Remote agents
evidence.finding: Group Chat moderators coordinate named local/remote agents. By default busy agents wait up to 15 minutes; disabling that safeguard permits concurrent file edits without a lock. Chat queues persist across reload/quit, restart paused, and retain failed sends until manual resume. Group chats can be deleted with their conversation history.

evidence.title: Maestro docs/autorun-playbooks.md
evidence.locator: Creating Tasks; Running Multiple Auto Run Documents; How a Goal Run Stops; Steering a Run in Flight; Auto-Resume After an Error; Human-in-the-Loop Gates; Stalled Documents; Halt Marker
evidence.finding: Goal runs stop on completion, deadlock, finite iteration cap or three stalled iterations. Desktop HITL markers pause until Done, Resume; CLI emits document_gated and skips the document. Three no-progress dispatches abandon a document. Halt markers stop the playbook and prevent replay until removed. Per-run auto-resume defaults to five attempts. Steering notes typed in the Thought Stream are delivered at the start of the next task. Checkboxes and the editor reopen while a run is paused; Reset on Completion keeps working copies in runs/.

evidence.title: Maestro docs/history.md
evidence.locator: Entry types; Validated flag; Storage; Cross-host history
evidence.finding: History links summaries, session IDs, timestamps and output. Validated is only a personal bookmark, not an execution gate. Entries can be deleted. JSON history defaults to 10000 entries per session; cross-host shared history is enabled per session through SSH Remote Execution.

evidence.title: Maestro docs/configuration.md
evidence.finding: Update-linked anonymous check-ins exclude prompts, agent output, file paths and project names. Disabling startup update checks disables check-ins. Optional cloud-folder sync includes settings/sessions/groups; simultaneous devices can conflict with last write winning and no conflict resolution.

evidence.title: Maestro Before you start; Operate; Known limits
evidence.locator: Before you start; Operate; Known limits
evidence.finding: Cue can run exported pipelines on Linux/systemd or containers without a desktop or logged-in user. Agents use server-side logins and YOLO permissions. Run database stores activity without output; engine logs hold output. In-flight runs become failed after engine restart. Stopping SSH shell steps stops the SSH client, not the remote command.

evidence.title: Maestro Overview; Available tools; Technical details
evidence.finding: Mintlify-hosted public read-only MCP exposes SearchMaestro for documentation search/retrieval, not session/task control. HTTP transport needs no authentication.

evidence.title: Maestro homepage
evidence.locator: 'The stage door' section; Legal footer (AGPL-3.0 License link); 'Elsewhere' (maestro-p)
evidence.finding: Says Maestro is open source under AGPL-3.0. Downloads come from GitHub Releases, and the page shows no price or pricing page. maestro-p is described as running claude -p on your own Claude Max quota.

evidence.title: Maestro docs index
evidence.finding: The docs index describes running several accounts of the same provider and spreading work across their plan quotas, so model usage stays on your own provider accounts. No pricing page is listed.

evidence.title: RunMaestro/Maestro LICENSE (AGPL-3.0)
evidence.finding: The code is published under AGPL-3.0. That license is about freedom to use, modify and share the code. It does not state a price.

evidence.title: Maestro agent ID list
evidence.finding: The canonical agent ID list at v1.0.2 includes claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, antigravity, qwen3-coder, opencode, factory-droid, hermes, pi, copilot-cli, omp and grok.

evidence.title: Maestro Pi agent definition
evidence.finding: The visible Pi definition spawns the pi binary in JSON output mode with session resume, read-only tool restriction and model override.

evidence.title: Maestro Grok CLI agent definition
evidence.finding: The visible Grok CLI definition spawns the grok binary in batch mode with streaming JSON output and resume; there is no interactive PTY integration.

evidence.title: Maestro Gemini CLI agent definition
evidence.finding: The gemini-cli definition is marked hidden and commented as not shipping, superseded by Antigravity, and kept only for type compatibility.

evidence.title: Maestro README supported agents
evidence.finding: README lists the supported coding CLIs and says Gemini CLI support is planned based on user demand, i.e. not currently supported. Line 106 repeats that Gemini CLI may be added in future releases.

evidence.title: Maestro provider notes: Pi
evidence.finding: Documents Pi provider features (image attachments, session resume, read-only mode, cost tracking, model selection) and that Maestro uses Pi's JSON output mode.

evidence.title: Maestro Cue overview
evidence.finding: Cue is an event-driven automation engine, on by default, that sends prompts to agents when file changes, timers, agent completions, GitHub activity or pending tasks fire, defined as subscriptions in .maestro/cue.yaml.

evidence.title: Maestro Cue time triggers
evidence.finding: time.heartbeat fires on a repeating interval and catches up after system sleep; time.scheduled is a cron-like trigger for specific times and weekdays.

evidence.title: Maestro Cue GitHub trigger
evidence.finding: The github.pull_request event polls GitHub for new pull requests via the gh CLI and triggers a subscription prompt; github.issue, github.label and webhook.received events follow in the same file.

evidence.title: Maestro Cue concurrency control
evidence.finding: max_concurrent limits parallel Cue runs per agent (default 1, so events run one at a time); extra events are queued up to queue_size and overflow is dropped with a toast.

evidence.title: Maestro README license
evidence.finding: README states the project is under the AGPL-3.0 licence and does not mention any paid tier or price.

evidence.title: Maestro v1.0.2 release assets
evidence.locator: GitHub release v1.0.2 assets: maestro-1.0.2-arm64-mac.dmg, maestro-1.0.2-x64-mac.dmg, Maestro-Setup-1.0.2-x64.exe, Maestro-Portable-1.0.2-x64.exe, maestro-1.0.2-x86_64.AppImage, .deb, .rpm
evidence.finding: The latest stable release publishes free downloadable installers for macOS, Windows and Linux on GitHub Releases.

evidence.title: Maestro v1.0.0 release notes
evidence.locator: GitHub release v1.0.0 notes, providers paragraph
evidence.finding: v1.0.0 release notes say Antigravity CLI, Grok CLI, Hermes, Oh My Pi and Pi joined the providers, running locally or over SSH.

evidence.title: Maestro website
evidence.finding: The website describes Maestro as open source under AGPL-3.0, downloaded from GitHub Releases, and shows no prices, paid plans, tiers, native phone apps, cloud service or team/SSO features.

evidence.title: Maestro Antigravity support at v1.0.2
evidence.finding: Maestro v1.0.2 ships Antigravity CLI as an agy provider with headless stream-json output, conversation resume and permission-mode arguments.

evidence.title: Maestro Antigravity support at v1.0.2
evidence.finding: Maestro v1.0.2 ships Antigravity CLI as an agy provider with headless stream-json output, conversation resume and permission-mode arguments.

evidence.title: Maestro remote control
evidence.finding: Multiple people can drive the same Maestro through optional Web Login. Browser prompts have per-user attribution and independent active tabs. The documentation explicitly says there are no roles; every account is an equal operator.

evidence.title: Maestro web login store
evidence.finding: The scoped web authentication implementation persists local username/password accounts and browser sessions. Inspection of src/main/web-server/auth and routes/authRoutes.ts for SSO, SAML, OIDC and OAuth found no identity-provider login implementation.

evidence.title: Maestro process manager
evidence.locator: spawn dispatch, lines 224-262; spawners/ChildProcessSpawner.ts lines 380-385; runners/SshCommandRunner.ts
evidence.finding: Agent launch selects local PTY/child processes or SSH commands on a user-configured host. The inspected process-manager spawners and runners do not provision a vendor runtime or per-agent containers or VMs. A user may separately choose to run its host in a VM or container.

evidence.title: Maestro distribution targets
evidence.locator: Electron build mac, win and linux targets; docs/remote-control.md Mobile Web Interface
evidence.finding: The scoped distribution builds Electron desktop packages for macOS, Windows and Linux. The phone client is the built-in browser interface; no native iOS or Android package exists in the inspected build targets.

evidence.title: Maestro provider notes
evidence.finding: Claude Code can use the user subscription login or an API key, gateway or cloud-provider credential in the agent environment; API credentials are billed by their provider.
